chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The Tashahhud in the prayer?' He said, 'Twice.' I said, 'And how is it twice?' He said, 'When you are seated upright, say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. Then you turn (to conclude).' I said, 'The saying of the servant: All greetings, prayers, and good things are for Allah.' He said, 'This is the gentleness of the supplication; Allah gentles the servant through it.'

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَس: I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger; the declaration of prophethood.
key_terms.أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; the core declaration of monotheism.
key_terms.التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ: All greetings are for Allah; the opening of the longer Tashahhud.
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: The sitting testimony in prayer, involving declarations of faith and greetings.
key_terms.اللُّطْفُ: Gentleness; referring to the divine ease or softening of the heart through supplication.
key_terms.مَرَّتَيْنِ: Twice; indicating the number of times the Tashahhud is recited.

ai.seo_question: How many times should the Tashahhud be recited in prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Tashahhud is recited twice, distinguishing the concise declaration of faith from the fuller 'Tahiyyat' as a specific divine grace ('al-lutf') that softens the worshipper's heart. This narration highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of supplication within the ritual structure, where the length of the testimony serves as a means of divine mercy rather than mere legal obligation. It underscores the theological concept that Allah's gentleness towards the servant is manifested through the richness of their devotional expressions.
